title: jevbox
blurb: A 3D boxing game where Jev calls every shot live. Pick two fighters Street Fighter-style, hit FIGHT, and watch them go at it.

media.alt: JEVBOX demo: exchange, super move, knockdown, TKO

title: Algoscope
blurb: 27 classic algorithms drawn live in SVG, with the code lighting up line by line next to them. Pause, rewind, set breakpoints, or feed it your own test cases.

media.alt: Algoscope landing page with a live BFS graph and bubble-sort bars

title: NeuroCraft
blurb: Type 'a castle on that hill' and a castle shows up on the hill. You describe a 3D world and it builds it.

media.alt: Typing 'a castle on the hill over there' makes a castle appear on a hill; the dragon grows and circles it; a wolf pack roams nearby; the world turns to golden sunset

title: Hollow Hand
blurb: A tarot deckbuilder where you play against Jev, a masked dealer who learns how you play and starts writing new rules to beat you.

media.alt: Gameplay: map, a full hand against The Fool, Jev's turn, the mask breaking

title: jevbrowser
blurb: A Chrome side panel that fills in job applications for me in my own logged-in browser. No screenshots, no vision model, and it always stops before hitting submit.

media.alt: The extension's side panel filling a job application (16 fields, then OVER TO YOU for the emailed verification code), then answering a five-question quiz and stopping at Submit answers

title: jevis
blurb: A voice assistant for Windows that reads the UI tree instead of squinting at pixels. My everyday commands never touch a model.

media.alt: jevis driving Calculator and Notepad from four spoken commands

title: Backlot
blurb: Local image gen with a recurring cast and a guided camera, so the same characters show up shot after shot. Runs Qwen-Image-2.1 on an 8GB GPU.

media.alt: Backlot demo: build a cast member, compose a shot, watch the pipeline, make it night

title: LeetGraph
blurb: LeetCode, but it's a roguelike. Pick a company, climb a map of its real interview questions, and let the game guilt you into coming back.

media.alt: Solving a node: confetti, rating tick, new paths unlock
slay-lc demo
packetsio-frontend demo

title: packetsio
blurb: A tick-based network packet simulator: Rust engine compiled to WebAssembly, packets as glowing particles. Switch between OSPF, adaptive and RIP routing and watch queues fill and tail-drop.

media.alt: packetsio demo

title: dogin
blurb: Password login built by hand in Rust (Axum, SQLite, Argon2, session cookies), with a live inspector that shows what the server did on every request.

media.alt: demo

title: boogle
blurb: My own tiny search engine in Rust. Stemming, TF-IDF ranking, and a UI that shows its maths for every result.

media.alt: Boogle demo: searching and opening the explain panel

title: Discorb
blurb: A mini Discord in Rust. Tokio, WebSockets, one broadcast channel per room, and the same binary serves the web client.

media.alt: Three users chatting in real time, switching rooms and surviving a server restart

title: zippy
blurb: A Huffman compressor in Rust, plus a visualizer that replays every step so you can watch 'abracadabra' turn into bits.

media.alt: zippy visualizer: counting bytes, merging the priority queue into a tree, reading codes and emitting bits

title: CLI Todo App
blurb: A simple command-line todo application written in Rust. This is my first Rust project, built to practice basic Rust concepts such as file I/O, error propagation, collections, and command-line input handling.

media.alt: cli-todo-app demo

title: Stuff3D
blurb: A 3D wireframe renderer in about 300 lines of C++. SFML opens the window and draws lines. The rotation, camera, clipping and perspective maths is all mine.

media.alt: Stuff3D running: walking around and through the penguin model

title: MLFQ Scheduler
blurb: A C++ sim of a multi-level feedback queue CPU scheduler, with a visualizer that replays it tick by tick.

media.alt: Demo: the visualizer playing a trace

title: Memory Management
blurb: Three C++ allocators for game objects (a bump arena, a fixed-slot pool and a ref-counted world with generation-checked handles), plus a page that replays a real run byte by byte.

media.alt: Visualizer replaying a trace: arena bump pointer, pool free stack, world handles and the dungeon view

title: DataFrame
blurb: A pandas-style DataFrame library in C++20: columnar storage, zero-copy views, group-by and hash join. The browser playground animates what every operation does.

media.alt: Playground demo: filter, select, sort, group-by and join on the sales dataset

title: OrderBook
blurb: A limit order book and matching engine in C++17 with price-time priority, market orders, cancels, modifies and GTC/IOC/FOK. Every fill gets recorded so you can replay it in the browser.

media.alt: Replaying a trace: orders queue at a level, fill FIFO, sweep the book

title: JsonParser
blurb: A recursive-descent JSON parser in C++17. It tells you the exact line and column you broke, and records every step so you can watch it parse.

media.alt: Visualizer replaying a parse: source cursor on the left, call stack in the middle, JsonValue tree on the right

title: Financr
blurb: A rental finance app for tenants and landlords: rent plans, bills, budgets, a rewards shop and an AI assistant that reads your own spending. Built over one hackathon weekend.

media.alt: Demo: landing page, tenant dashboard, setting a budget, accepting a rent plan, redeeming a reward, asking the AI assistant

title: TrippAI
blurb: Pick a city and it tells you which week of the next year to go. Prophet forecasts for weather, crowds and price, reweighted live on a month-by-month heatmap.

media.alt: TrippAI demo

title: LeadGreen
blurb: A sustainability game for campus: scan a QR code where you did something green, post a photo, earn points, grow a plant. Uni group project, team of nine. I built most of the plant game frontend.

media.alt: LeadGreen demo

title: FireLine
blurb: Seventy years of California wildfires on a satellite map. Start a fire anywhere and watch it spread with live weather, or ask a small neural net how a house would fare. Built in a day at HackSW.

media.alt: FireLine demo

title: Card Game Threads
blurb: A multithreaded card game in Java: every player is a thread passing cards round a ring of locked decks until someone holds four of a kind. The visualiser replays real runs.

media.alt: Replay of a 4-player game, then an 8-player game

title: Battleships
blurb: Battleships against three AIs in Python and Flask. Drag your fleet on, trade shots, watch ships sink. My first-year coursework, rebuilt properly in 2026.

media.alt: Placing ships and playing a few turns against the expert AI

title: WasteLess
blurb: Track the food in your kitchen, catch it before it expires, and find recipes that use it up. Four of us built it in four days at a Google DevFest hackathon.

media.alt: WasteLess demo
